title: AI Governance Workflow with Interactive Details
subtitle: From use-case proposal through ethics review, deployment, and post-launch monitoring

flow.title: Submit Use Case
flow.meaning: A business owner formally submits a new AI use case, documenting its purpose, data sources, and expected business impact.
flow.inputDesc: Business context, problem statement, success metrics
flow.example: Marketing team submits a proposal to use NLP for customer sentiment analysis on support tickets to improve response routing.

flow.title: Risk Classification
flow.meaning: An automated system evaluates the use case against regulatory frameworks and internal risk taxonomies to assign a governance tier.
flow.inputDesc: Use case intake form, training data lineage, stakeholders
flow.outputDesc: Risk tier classification, in-scope data map
flow.example: Use case intake form → Risk tier classification

flow.title: Ethics Review
flow.meaning: A cross-functional ethics committee reviews the classified use case for bias, fairness concerns, and privacy implications.
flow.inputDesc: Risk tier classification, training data analysis, model card
flow.example: Committee examines whether sentiment model has bias against non-English speakers, and ensures ticket routing decisions have human override capability.

flow.title: Approved?
flow.meaning: A binary decision gate: proceed to deployment or request modifications.
flow.example: If bias concerns are identified, the decision routes to 'Rejected' with conditions; if none, routing is approved.

flow.title: Deploy Model
flow.meaning: The approved model is registered in the model registry, cryptographically signed, and released to production via canary deployment.
flow.inputDesc: Approved model artifacts, deployment plan, infrastructure configs
flow.outputDesc: Signed model artifact, live endpoint, audit trail
flow.example: The sentiment model is registered in the internal model registry, signed with the deployment certificate, and rolled out to 5% of production traffic for validation.

flow.title: Monitor & Audit
flow.meaning: Continuous monitoring detects model performance drift, fairness degradation, and anomalies; all predictions are audit-logged.
flow.inputDesc: Live model predictions, ground truth labels, user feedback
flow.outputDesc: Performance metrics, drift alerts, audit logs
flow.example: Daily dashboards track model accuracy on ticket sentiment, detecting any drift in non-English text handling. Every routing decision is logged immutably.

loops.label: drift detected → re-classify
loops.meaning: If monitoring detects performance drift or fairness issues, the use case is re-classified and re-reviewed before continuing.
